title: Worked Examples — Correction Charge by Days Since the State's Response (Cardinal Financial Responsibility Filing)
content:
## Rule

For a corrected refiling of a Cardinal Financial Responsibility Filing certificate, the correction charge follows the calendar days from the response date of the latest state response on the filing's record to today:

- **2 days or fewer:** the correction is not charged; the correction charge is 0.00.
- **More than 2 days and no more than 6 days:** the correction charge is the correction rate multiplied by those days and divided by the certificate's rejection correction days (10 calendar days on every certificate), rounded up to the cent.
- **More than 6 days:** the correction charge is the correction rate as it stands.

## Day-by-day examples (hypothetical rates)

| Days since the latest state response | Correction rate 10.00 | Correction rate 20.00 |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.00 | 0.00 |
| 2 | 0.00 | 0.00 |
| 3 | 3.00 (10.00 multiplied by 3, divided by 10) | 6.00 |
| 5 | 5.00 | 10.00 |
| 6 | 6.00 | 12.00 |
| 7 | 10.00 | 20.00 |

## Rounding up (hypothetical rate)

With a correction rate taken, for illustration only, as 12.35 and 3 days elapsed: 12.35 multiplied by 3 is 37.05; divided by 10 is 3.705; rounded up to the cent, **3.71**.

## Which response

The latest state response on the filing's record sets the start date, and that response date is day 0. A response dated 4 May gives 2 days on 6 May (not charged), 3 days on 7 May (prorated) and 7 days on 11 May (full rate).
